key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and uncover high-efficiency, lead-free device designs.
engineering_relevance: The study provides actionable design rules for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL materials to improve efficiency while reducing the need for exhaustive device-by-device simulation or experiment.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP analysis to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance, and the top designs achieved 28.85% PCE for FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag and 28.62% for FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag.
watch_item: The model’s reliability depends on the representativeness of the simulated training set, so extrapolation beyond the explored material space should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
